title: Barazek (Damascus sesame and pistachio cookies)
steps: Make a light syrup by simmering the 100 g sugar and water for 5 minutes, then cool it completely.
Cream the butter and sugar until pale, then add the milk and orange blossom water, followed by the flour and baking powder, mixing to a soft dough.
Shape the dough into small balls the size of a walnut and flatten them into thin ovals.
Spread the sesame seeds on a plate, dip one side of each cookie in the cool syrup, then press that side into the sesame so it is fully coated.
Place the cookies sesame-side up on a lined tray and press a few pistachio halves on top.
Bake at 180 C for 15 to 18 minutes until pale golden and the sesame is toasted. Cool on the tray.

title: Cherry kebab (Aleppo meatballs in sour cherry sauce)

ingredients.name: pitted sour cherries (fresh, or jarred and drained)

steps: Mix the lamb with the grated onion, allspice, salt and pepper and knead well. Shape into walnut-sized balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil in a wide pan in batches and set aside.
Add the cherries, sugar and stock to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes until the cherries release their juice and turn the sauce deep magenta.
Return the meatballs, add the pomegranate molasses, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the sauce thickens and the meat is cooked through.
Taste and balance sweet against sour with more sugar or molasses.
Serve over flatbread or rice and scatter with pine nuts.

title: Fatayer (Syrian spinach and sumac pies)

ingredients.name: fresh spinach, chopped (or 250 g frozen, squeezed dry)

steps: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, oil and warm water into a soft dough for 8 minutes, cover, and let it rise for 1 hour.
Mix the chopped spinach with the onion, sumac, lemon juice, olive oil and a pinch of salt, and squeeze out excess liquid.
Roll the dough out thinly and cut it into circles 10 cm across.
Put a spoonful of filling in the centre of each circle and pinch the edges together in three places to form a triangle, sealing the seams well.
Place on a lined tray and bake at 200 C for 18 to 20 minutes until golden.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Fatteh (Syrian chickpea, toasted bread and yogurt platter)
steps: Toast the torn pita in the oven at 200 C for 8 to 10 minutes, or fry it in oil, until crisp and golden.
Whisk the yogurt with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice and a little salt until smooth and pourable.
Warm the chickpeas in a little of their cooking liquid with the cumin and salt.
Spread the crisp bread on a deep platter, moisten with a few spoonfuls of the chickpea liquid, then layer the chickpeas and the yogurt sauce on top.
Melt the butter in a small pan, fry the pine nuts until golden, stir in the paprika, and pour the sizzling butter over the platter.
Scatter with parsley and serve immediately, before the bread softens completely.

title: Halawet el jibn (Syrian sweet cheese rolls with cream)

ingredients.name: low-moisture mozzarella (or akkawi, soaked and drained), shredded
thick cream (ashta, clotted cream or mascarpone), sweetened to taste

steps: Make the syrup by simmering the 150 g sugar with its water for 8 minutes, stirring in the rose water at the end, and let it cool.
Bring the 350 ml water and the tablespoon of sugar to the boil and stir in the semolina, cooking for a few minutes until thick.
Add the shredded cheese and orange blossom water and stir over low heat until the cheese melts and the mix forms a smooth, stretchy dough.
Turn the warm dough onto a surface dusted with sugar or lightly oiled, and roll or press it into a thin rectangle about 3 mm thick.
Spread the cream over it, roll up tightly like a log, and cut into thick slices.
Chill the slices for an hour, drizzle with the cool syrup, and finish with ground pistachios.

title: Kibbeh (Syrian fried bulgur and lamb torpedoes)

ingredients.name: lean lamb, trimmed and minced twice (or beef)
oil, plus oil for deep frying

steps: Make the filling first. Fry the chopped onion in 3 tablespoons of oil until golden, add the ground lamb and cook until browned, then add the pine nuts, a teaspoon of allspice, salt, pepper and pomegranate molasses. Cool completely.
Work the soaked bulgur, minced lamb, grated onion, salt, allspice and cinnamon together in a food processor with a few splashes of iced water until it forms a smooth, pliable paste.
With wet hands take a golf-ball-sized piece, poke a hole in it with your finger and work it into a thin-walled cup.
Fill the cup with a spoonful of the cooled filling and pinch the opening closed, shaping into a torpedo with pointed ends.
Heat the frying oil to about 175 C and fry the kibbeh in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until dark golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with yogurt and a salad.

title: Kibbeh safarjaliyeh (Aleppo quince and kibbeh stew)

ingredients.name: lamb or beef, cut into chunks
quinces, peeled, cored and cut into wedges
lean minced lamb, for the kibbeh
ground lamb, cooked with onion and spices, for filling
salt, pepper and allspice to taste

steps: Brown the lamb chunks with the chopped onion in the oil, then cover with about 750 ml of water, add salt and pepper, and simmer for 1 hour.
Fry the quince wedges in a little oil until golden, then add them to the pot with the pomegranate juice, molasses and sugar.
Make small kibbeh balls: knead the bulgur with the lean minced lamb, salt and allspice into a paste, shape into walnut-sized cups, fill each with a little cooked spiced mince, and seal.
Simmer the stew for another 30 minutes until the quince is tender but not collapsed and the broth is slightly sweet and sour.
Drop the kibbeh balls into the simmering broth and cook for 10 minutes until firm.
Adjust the sweet and sour balance and serve in bowls with rice.

title: Maarouk (Syrian sweet Ramadan bread)

ingredients.name: egg yolk beaten with a little milk, for glaze

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and aniseed in a large bowl and add the butter and warm milk.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and soft, then cover and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 2 pieces, shape each into a long loaf or oval, and place on a lined tray.
Let rise again for 30 minutes, then brush with the egg glaze and sprinkle with the seeds.
Bake at 190 C for 25 to 30 minutes until golden brown.
Cool slightly and serve sliced, with cheese, jam or sweet cream for the Ramadan meal.

title: Muhammara (Aleppo red pepper and walnut dip)

ingredients.name: large red bell peppers, roasted and peeled (or 250 g jarred roasted red peppers)
Aleppo pepper (or chilli flakes plus a little paprika)

steps: Roast the peppers over a flame or under a grill until blackened, put them in a covered bowl to steam, then peel and deseed them.
Pulse the walnuts with the breadcrumbs, garlic, cumin and chilli to a coarse crumb.
Add the peppers, pomegranate molasses and lemon juice and blend to a thick, slightly textured paste.
With the machine running, drizzle in the olive oil and season with salt.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with more olive oil, and serve with warm flatbread and raw vegetables.

title: Qamar al-din (Syrian apricot drink)

ingredients.name: qamar al-din apricot sheets (or soft apricot fruit leather)

steps: Tear the apricot sheets into pieces and soak them in the water for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Blend the soaked apricot and its water until completely smooth.
Strain the drink through a sieve to remove any fibre.
Stir in the sugar and orange blossom water until dissolved, adding more water if the drink is too thick.
Chill thoroughly and serve cold in tall glasses, traditionally at the end of the fast during Ramadan.

title: Qatayef (Syrian stuffed pancakes with walnuts and syrup)

ingredients.name: rose water or orange blossom water

steps: Make the syrup by simmering the 200 g sugar, water and lemon juice for 10 minutes, then stirring in the rose water and cooling.
Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar, baking powder, salt and warm water into a smooth, thin batter and leave it for 30 minutes.
Cook small spoonfuls of batter in a lightly greased non-stick pan over medium heat, one side only, until the surface is covered with bubbles and set. Do not flip them.
Mix the walnuts with the filling sugar and cinnamon.
Put a spoonful of filling on the cooked side of each pancake, fold it into a half-moon and pinch the edges to seal.
Fry the stuffed pancakes in oil until golden (or brush with butter and bake at 200 C for 12 minutes), then dip them in the cool syrup and serve.

title: Shaifura (Syrian shanklish, tomato and onion salad)

ingredients.name: shanklish (or crumbled feta mixed with a little dried thyme)

steps: Crumble the cheese into a bowl with your fingers.
Add the tomatoes, onion, green pepper and parsley.
Pour in the olive oil and toss everything together gently.
Sprinkle with mint or Aleppo pepper and serve with flatbread for scooping.

title: Shakriyeh (Syrian lamb in warm yogurt sauce)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or leg, in chunks (bone-in if possible)
cornflour (cornstarch), mixed with 2 tbsp cold water

steps: Put the lamb, onion, cinnamon and cardamom in a pot with water to cover and a good pinch of salt. Simmer gently for 1.5 hours until very tender, skimming the surface.
Drain the meat and keep about 250 ml of the broth.
In a separate pot, whisk the yogurt, cornflour mixture and egg white until perfectly smooth.
Heat the yogurt over medium-low heat, stirring constantly in one direction, until it comes to a gentle simmer. Keep stirring to prevent it from splitting and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the lamb and enough of the reserved broth to loosen the sauce, and simmer very gently for 15 to 20 minutes, adding salt to taste.
Serve over rice with ghee-toasted pine nuts on top.

title: Sheikh al-mahshi (Syrian stuffed courgettes in yogurt sauce)
steps: Trim the courgettes and hollow out each with a corer, leaving a thin wall and keeping the end intact.
Fry the onion in the oil until golden, add the lamb and brown it, then stir in the pine nuts, allspice, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Stuff the courgettes loosely with the filling and brown them lightly in a pan.
Whisk the yogurt with the cornflour and a little water, bring it to a gentle simmer over low heat stirring constantly in one direction, and add salt.
Lay the courgettes in the yogurt sauce, cover, and simmer on low for 25 to 30 minutes until tender.
Fry the garlic and dried mint briefly in a little oil and pour over the dish before serving with rice.
